title: Claude Code config tests must clear MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING between cases
answers: config test leaks async trace logging env var between tests
ensureInitialized test passes or fails depending on order
how to write a Claude Code config test that checks env defaults
body:
Invariant: ensureInitialized writes MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING into process.env, so the value persists across tests in the same process.
Enforced by: libs/typescript/integrations/claude-code/tests/config.test.ts, the beforeEach block that deletes process.env entries (including MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING) before each case.
What breaks if skipped: a case that expects the unset-default 'true' can see 'false' or 'true' left over from an earlier opt-out or opt-in case, so results depend on test order.
Convention: When adding an env-default test, set the variable explicitly for the opt-out or opt-in case, and add any new env var to that cleanup list.
applies: Applies to tests in the Claude Code integration package that call ensureInitialized.
says: Verify that background trace recording in Claude Code remains enabled when left unconfigured.
Test that opting out of asynchronous trace collection in Claude Code disables tracking properly.
Ensure automated validation of default background tracing settings in Claude Code runs reliably.
search: Claude Code configuration tests in libs/typescript/integrations/claude-code/tests/config.test.ts must clear MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING from process.env in beforeEach to prevent test pollution. Calling ensureInitialized writes the variable into process.env, which otherwise leaks into subsequent tests and causes cases expecting the unset-default 'true' to depend on execution order. New environment-default tests must set variables explicitly for opt-in or opt-out cases and register any new variable in the cleanup list.
